body:
## Tier header
- **Tier: T4.** Why: consent copy that clients agree to (box 2, WA MHMDA consumer health data), consent version semantics, and destructive data changes (a client delete hard-deletes Roman transcripts; fix round 2 adds delete-all).
- **T4 trigger scan:** consent/PII copy and version (yes); destructive data (yes: `RomanMessage` hard delete on client request, `DELETE /roman/sessions` erases every chat of the caller, and the sweep erases deleted-but-unerased pre-upgrade sessions); auth/RLS/tenancy (fix round 2: three routes move to a controller outside `RomanFeatureGuard`, still JwtAuthGuard + RolesGuard; every read and erase is scoped by session id AND user_id; the erase now verifies zero messages remain, so an RLS-blocked delete is a coded 503, not a silent 204; no RLS or policy change); CI gate files (fix round 1 added one step at the end of `mwb-3-live-tests`; fix round 2 changes no CI file); money/credentials/migrations (none).
- **T3 trigger scan:** cross-repo contract (yes: mobile #310/#326 send `client-ai-v4` and its sha256; fix round 2 adds `GET /roman/sessions`, `DELETE /roman/sessions` for a mobile delete-chat screen, documented in `docs/roman-chat-deletion.md`); scheduled job (`RomanErasureSweep`, boot + 04:00 UTC + bounded follow-ups); no schema/migration change.
- **Bounded T1:** none.
- **Builder-owner:** lane B-CONSENT-COPY (agent 110) for 0a32b4fe; fix round 1 (B-635-1, C-635-1) by lane B-CONSENT-2 (agent 111); fix round 2 (B-635-2, B-635-3, C-635-1..3) by lane B-CONSENT-3 (agent 111). Operator merges.
- **Promotion triggers:** none above T4.
- **Acceptance evidence:** see "Acceptance evidence (head c2688010)" below; CI at head is the merge gate.

## Why
Owner 2026-10-01 20:32: "I want to keep past AI chats forever." Operator ruling OR-110-1: a client-initiated chat delete and account deletion still erase them (legal deletion rights; App Store 5.1.1(v)); privacy wording "kept until you delete them or your account". The box-2 server copy `client-ai-v3` said Roman chats are "kept for 180 days, and you can delete them at any time". No purge exists, so the consent text misstated retention (AUD-OPUS-2 R-626-1 on #626, B-310-6 on mobile #310, Sol's release note on #326).

Also found: on main `DELETE /roman/sessions/:id` was a SOFT delete (messages stayed in the database). "Kept until you delete them" would still be false, so this PR makes the client delete erase.

## What changed
1. **Copy bump to `client-ai-v4`** (`src/ai-consent/ai-consent.constants.ts`). The only text change is the last sentence of paragraph 4:
   - v3: "Your conversations with Roman are private from your coach, kept for 180 days, and you can delete them at any time."
   - v4: "Your conversations with Roman are private from your coach and are kept until you delete them or delete your account."
   - Box label unchanged. New digests: paragraph `56d14fb96b9f7b6abdd43242f5ce9eaee419bc0d9fb4302bc283ecc1529d430b`, label `77da153df7f06a045e1abbbb83b771f8a33941d47268e276becc6b4ffe5e5eba`, combined `copy_sha256` `fbf821401d4313c6a301a6cc08d3870bb117c293fbb970e321bf87f49abe34f4`.
2. **How v3 grants are treated: the existing exact-match rule, unchanged** (no special case added):
   - a v3 (or older) grant stays in the append-only history and is never rewritten;
   - it is not consent: `GET /me/ai-consent` shows `state: needs_reconsent`, `granted: false`; `hasClientAiConsent()` is false; every AI path refuses with `ai_consent_required` until the client allows the v4 text (the #326 sheet and #310 Settings show the server's v4 copy for that);
   - `POST /me/ai-consent/roman` naming `client-ai-v3` (or v4 with the v3 sha256) is 409 `CONSENT_VERSION_MISMATCH`; nothing is written;
   - `DELETE` while the latest decision is a v3 grant records the withdraw against `client-ai-v3`;
   - why no compat window: the v3 text promised 180-day deletion, which is not what happens, so a v3 grant is not consent to the real retention. No shipped mobile build posts v3 (#310 is unmerged; #326 posts whatever the server serves). Same pattern as the operator's consult-consent ruling ("no live v1 clients; no compat window").
3. **Client delete erases the conversation** (`src/roman/roman.service.ts` `deleteSession`, was `softDeleteSession`). One transaction, scoped to the caller's session id AND user_id:
   - tombstone the session row (`deleted_at`, `subject_context_json` cleared);
   - hard-delete every `RomanMessage` of the session;
   - keep only a content-free count of the user turns that were inside the rolling 24h window, so deleting a chat never resets the daily Roman cap (`assertWithinRateLimit` adds it back while the erased session is recent).
   - `appendMessage` now bumps the live session first (`updateMany` where `deleted_at: null` and `user_id`) and is a 404 when the session was deleted, so a streamed reply that finishes after the delete is never stored. The row lock orders a racing append and delete.
4. **No 180-day purge job or retention config exists on main** (searched `src`, `env-validation.ts`, `.env.example`, docs): nothing to remove. `.env.example` and `docs/ai-consent-ledger.md` updated to v4, with the v3 rule written out.

## Account deletion (the "or delete your account" half)
Main's legacy deletion paths (`account-deletion.service.ts` finalize, `GdprScrubService`) do not touch Roman tables. Backend #608 (open) erases `RomanMessage` and `RomanSession` by `user_id` in its erasure manifest (`account-deletion.manifest.ts:185-187`). Release dependency: the v4 copy goes live with or after #608, which is already the ship order for #611 and mobile #313. This PR does not touch the deletion service, to avoid conflicting with #608.

## Merge order / coordination
- Mobile #310 (P0 box 2 + Settings) and #326 (consent sheet) carry the matching `client-ai-v4` constants and pins. Deploy this backend before, or in the same window as, a build carrying #310. A build with v3 constants would get 409 on every box-2 grant against this backend; a v4 build against an old backend would also get 409. Neither blocks onboarding (box 2 is optional, and the 409 is handled as "not saved").
- Backend #611 privacy text states the same retention.
- Fix round 2 release items (operator routing; not in this PR): no mobile build has a delete-chat screen yet (`softDeleteRomanSession` is unused on mobile main, #310 and #326), so "kept until you delete them" needs a mobile delete affordance on these routes; "or delete your account" needs #608 deployed; the data export does not include Roman chats yet (B-EXPORT).

## Fix round 2 (Opus AUDIT 5956763748 A0/B1/C2, Sol AUDIT 5956842685 A0/B2/C3 @ e7f67576), head c2688010
Merged main e867fe62 (526036e8) and 3bd6215b (c2688010), both clean. Then 653a9bfb + 98af609e:
1. **B-635-2: the client can find and delete any chat.** New `RomanChatsController` (`src/roman/roman-chats.controller.ts`), JwtAuthGuard + RolesGuard, NOT behind `FEATURE_ROMAN_CHAT_ENABLED` (same rule as the consent ledger: the chat kill switch never takes a deletion right away), all `Cache-Control: no-store`, no Anthropic call:
   - `GET /roman/sessions?limit=&cursor=&surface=`: own live chats, newest first, keyset cursor; metadata only (id, surface, dayKey, messageCount, startedAt, lastActivityAt). A cursor that is not one of the caller's sessions is a 400 `ROMAN_CURSOR_INVALID`; a chat deleted between pages stays a valid cursor.
   - `DELETE /roman/sessions/:id` (moved from `RomanController`): erases a chat of any day.
   - `DELETE /roman/sessions`: erases every chat of the caller (both surfaces, every day, and the caller's own pre-#635 tombstones), one transaction per chat, 204 even when none. A failure part-way, or more than 50x100 chats, is a 503 `ROMAN_ERASE_INCOMPLETE`; erased chats stay erased, a retry finishes.
   - The daily cap is never reset (erased shells keep the content-free in-window count). Contract: `docs/roman-chat-deletion.md`.
   - Found while testing: `?limit=30` was a 400 on `GET /roman/sessions/:id/messages` (`@Transform` without implicit conversion ran after `@IsInt`); both Roman list DTOs now use `@Type(() => Number)`. That route is now `no-store` too (a deleted transcript does not stay in a device HTTP cache; it was `private, max-age=60`).
2. **B-635-3: sweep failures are sanitized, counted and alerted.** `RomanService.runUnerasedErasure` returns `{ erased, failed, firstFailure, boundHit }`; a per-row failure is logged through `safeDiagnostic` (no ORM text), the row is left for retry and the rest continue. `RomanErasureSweep` logs one line every run (`roman.erase_sweep trigger= erased= failed= remaining=`), sends one sanitized Sentry `RomanErasureIncomplete` summary when any row failed, and never throws.
3. **C-635-1: rollout completion is observable and self-finishing.** The sweep runs again 60 s later while it makes progress and rows remain; with no progress it retries every 15 min up to 4 times, then raises `RomanErasureStalled` and waits for the nightly run. The "first start clears every pre-upgrade row" comment is corrected. Operator qualification: a `remaining=0` log line, or `SELECT count(*) FROM "RomanSession" WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND day_key NOT LIKE 'erased:%'` = 0 (in the doc).
4. **C-635-2: coded, idempotent.** Every session-not-found is 404 `ROMAN_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` "This conversation no longer exists. Open Roman again to start a new one." (never 403). A repeat delete is a 204 and writes nothing; deleting the caller's own pre-#635 tombstone erases it; a delete that loses a race re-reads once.
5. **C-635-3: the erase is verified.** After `deleteMany` the transaction counts the session's messages; any left (an RLS-blocked delete removes zero rows without an error) is a 503 `ROMAN_ERASE_INCOMPLETE` and the transaction rolls back. An open whose legacy key holder cannot be erased answers its own 503 `ROMAN_UNAVAILABLE`.

## Acceptance evidence (local, heavy.sh, head c2688010)
- Failing before: the new and changed tests run against the e7f67576 `src/roman` (ts-jest diagnostics off so they run): 37 failed, including Sol's unmodified probe `635-q2-erasure-failure-probe.spec.ts` (2/2 failed).
- After: `env CI=false npx jest --runInBand --forceExit --runTestsByPath` on the Sol probe copy + `test/roman/{roman.service,roman-erasure.sweep,roman-chats.controller,roman.controller,roman-streaming,roman-sse-error-contract,roman.prompts,roman-session-erase.live}.spec.ts test/ai-consent/{ai-consent.service,ai-consent.controller,ai-consent-dunning-lockout.e2e}.spec.ts test/module-graph.spec.ts test/dunning-v2-lockout-allowlist-route-table.spec.ts test/dunning-v2-lockout-guard.e2e.spec.ts`: 14 suites passed, 276 tests passed, live suite skipped without a DB (no local Postgres this round). Then `roman.service.spec` 51/51 after 98af609e; `ai-egress-guard`, `support-email.guard`, `ai-consent-wiring`, `route-doc-drift`: 47/47. The probe copy was deleted, not committed.
- `roman-chats.controller.spec.ts` boots Nest over HTTP with the production ValidationPipe, HttpExceptionFilter and CacheControlInterceptor: list/delete/delete-all work with the flag OFF, `?limit=30` is a number, bad params are 400, coded 404/503 reach the wire, chat routes stay 404 while OFF.
- Live Postgres (CI `mwb-3-live-tests`, `MWB3_TEST_DATABASE_URL`): new cases for list paging + delete-all of prior-day and today chats on both surfaces (other user untouched, cap kept, foreign cursor 400), prior-day delete by id + repeat 204 + foreign 404, and the C-635-3 RLS probe (a NOBYPASSRLS role with a read policy and no DELETE policy; negative control proves its delete removes 0 rows silently; then delete is a coded 503 and the chat stays whole).
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3584 npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: exit 0. eslint on the 12 changed TS files: 0 problems. Prettier on new/clean files (roman.service/controller/dto and two specs are unformatted on main, not reformatted). `node scripts/check-r75.js --mode=range --base=origin/main --head=HEAD`: OK, no positive token change.
- No schema or migration change.

## Acceptance evidence (local, heavy.sh, head 0a32b4fe)
- `npx jest --runInBand --forceExit --runTestsByPath test/ai-consent/ai-consent.service.spec.ts test/ai-consent/ai-consent.controller.spec.ts test/ai-consent/ai-consent-dunning-lockout.e2e.spec.ts test/roman/roman.service.spec.ts test/roman/roman-streaming.spec.ts test/roman/roman.controller.spec.ts test/roman/roman-sse-error-contract.spec.ts`: 7 suites passed, 0 failed (ai-consent pair re-run after the last edit: 79/79).
- New tests: the v3 sha256 is proven to be the superseded 180-day text; the v3 grant gives needs_reconsent and reader false, and its row is never rewritten; POST v3 gives 409 in both the service and over HTTP (the HTTP envelope carries the code, and GET then serves v4); a v3 withdrawal is recorded against v3; re-consent appends a v4 grant. Roman: the delete hard-deletes every message and clears the subject context, and another user's chat is untouched; a non-owner delete is 404 with nothing erased; a second delete is 404; a late turn after the delete is refused and never stored; the cap is not reset by a delete; erased turns stop counting once outside the window.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3584 heavy.sh npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: 0 errors. eslint on 11 changed files: 0 problems. (roman.service.ts/controller.ts were not prettier-formatted on main either; not reformatted, to keep the diff reviewable.)
- No schema or migration change, so Schema parity is unaffected.

## Fix round 1 (Sol REQUEST CHANGES @ 0a32b4fe, comment 5955389344), head e7f67576
Merged main e5d10bd8 (merge commit b012ae99, no conflicts), then:
1. **B-635-1: a delete frees the same-day key** (`src/roman/roman.service.ts`). The unique index `roman_session_user_surface_day` (user_id, surface, day_key) covers deleted rows, so the tombstone blocked every fresh open with P2002 until UTC midnight. No schema change: inside the erase transaction the row moves to `day_key = erased:<session id>` (`erasedDayKey`, prefix `ROMAN_ERASED_DAY_KEY_PREFIX`), which is unique per session and never a calendar day.
   - Nothing is resurrected: the shell stays `deleted_at` set, holds no text and no subject context; `getOwnedSession` / `appendMessage` still 404 on it.
   - The cap is not reset: the shell keeps `message_count` = erased in-window user turns and its `last_activity_at`. `assertWithinRateLimit` now sums erased shells with a database `aggregate` (the old 16-row read bound could under-count once a user can delete many chats a day) and excludes unerased pre-upgrade rows, whose messages are already in the live count (no double count).
   - `openOrResumeSession` keeps the P2002 race recovery (re-find the live row). If no live row exists, an unerased deleted row holds today's key (pre-upgrade): it is erased, then the create is retried once. A second failure is a 503 `ROMAN_UNAVAILABLE` "Roman could not open a new conversation just now. Wait a moment and open Roman again."
2. **C-635-1: pre-upgrade tombstones are erased** (`src/roman/roman-erasure.sweep.ts`, `RomanService.eraseUnerasedDeletedSessions`). A deleted row whose day_key is still a calendar day was soft-deleted before this PR (or by an old machine during a rolling deploy) and still holds transcript and subject context. Same erasure as a client delete (messages hard-deleted, subject context cleared, content-free cap count kept, key released), per-row compare-and-set on (`deleted_at` not null, the original day_key), so several machines can run it and each row is erased once. Batches of 100, at most 50 per run; a failing row is logged and skipped, the rest continue.
   - Runs 60 s after boot (the first start of this version clears every pre-upgrade row) and nightly at 04:00 UTC (after the 03:00-03:45 deletion/export/scrub slots) for rollout stragglers. Never throws; a failed run goes to Sentry (`safeDiagnostic`). Runs regardless of `FEATURE_ROMAN_CHAT_ENABLED`.
   - It never touches a live session, so it is not a retention purge (owner: past AI chats are kept until the client deletes them or their account).
   - Production inventory: I have no production access, so I cannot prove it empty; the code handles any count.
3. **Tests against the real uniqueness contract.**
   - Unit fake (`test/roman/roman.service.spec.ts`) now enforces the unique key over all rows, deleted or not, and throws a real `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` P2002 (a negative-control test proves it). New blocks "same-day fresh session after a delete (B-635-1)" and "pre-upgrade soft-deleted sessions are erased (C-635-1)".
   - New live spec `test/roman/roman-session-erase.live.spec.ts` runs `RomanService` on real Postgres with the full Prisma schema (`bootstrapTestSchema`). Negative control: Postgres rejects a second row on a key a deleted row holds (P2002). Then open -> append -> delete -> open the same day (fresh, empty, takes turns); 6 concurrent opens after a delete converge on one live row; a late append to the deleted session is 404 and stores nothing; a delete racing an append leaves no transcript (5 rounds); delete + reopen keeps the cap (and another user is unaffected); a legacy tombstone holding today's key is erased on open; the sweep erases legacy rows, leaves the live chat, and is idempotent.
   - CI: the spec runs in a new final step of `mwb-3-live-tests` (own step, so it does not edit the shared default-lane list that #607 also extends). `roman-erasure.sweep.spec.ts` pins that step and the module provider.

## Acceptance evidence (local, heavy.sh, head e7f67576)
- `npx jest --runInBand --forceExit --runTestsByPath test/roman/roman.service.spec.ts test/roman/roman-erasure.sweep.spec.ts test/roman/roman-session-erase.live.spec.ts test/roman/roman.controller.spec.ts test/roman/roman-streaming.spec.ts test/roman/roman-sse-error-contract.spec.ts test/roman/roman.prompts.spec.ts test/ai-consent/ai-consent.service.spec.ts test/ai-consent/ai-consent.controller.spec.ts test/ai-consent/ai-consent-dunning-lockout.e2e.spec.ts test/module-graph.spec.ts`: 10 suites passed, 188 tests passed, live suite skipped without a DB (sweep spec then extended: 7/7).
- Live, real Postgres (local PostgreSQL 18.6 throwaway cluster; CI uses 15): `MWB3_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@localhost:55432/postgres npx jest --runInBand --forceExit --testTimeout=120000 --runTestsByPath test/roman/roman-session-erase.live.spec.ts`: 8/8 passed.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3584 npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: exit 0. eslint on the 8 changed TS files: 0 problems. Prettier on the new/clean files; roman.service.ts and the two Roman specs are unformatted on main and were not reformatted. `node scripts/check-r75.js --mode=range --base=origin/main --head=HEAD`: OK, no positive token change.
- No schema or migration change (schema parity unaffected; no migration prefix taken).

title: feat(ai-consent): client-ai-v4 true AI-chat retention copy; Roman delete erases the transcript (T4)
